title: Hybrid backpressure credit allocator for multipart requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multipart and long-lived requests (multipart uploads, interleaved streaming + file payloads, and chunked HTTP bodies) are producing incorrect usage accounting across the metering pipeline. Current model allocates final token credits at request start or on request termination only. When the client pauses, reconnects, or the system performs midstream model fallback, we see three classes of failures: 1) double-crediting when retries cause transient replays, 2) lost credits when partial payloads are accepted but finalization fails (no commit), and 3) premature quota enforcement that throttles in-flight work leading to user errors and refunds. This ticket proposes a hybrid backpressure credit allocator that uses provisional staged credits + periodic checkpoint commits to guarantee correct counting while keeping latency and memory use bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional credit allocations are recorded at request-chunk boundaries, not only at start or end
System can commit or rollback provisional credits deterministically on stream finalization or abort
Rate limiter honors provisional allocations against soft quotas but only reduces hard-commit quotas when a checkpoint is committed
Resume/retry scenarios do not result in >1x final credit for the same logical output in 99.999% of observed cases
End-to-end e2e tests for multipart uploads, client reconnects, and midstream model fallback pass in CI
Monitoring dashboards surface provisional vs committed credits and reconciliation errors < 0.01% of requests
design_notes: Introduce a lightweight provisional_credit record (request_id, provisional_tokens, checkpoint_id, timestamp) stored in the ephemeral metering cache (redis) with an optional durable tombstone in the accounting DB on commit
Use client-provided idempotency token + server-assigned checkpoint_id to deterministically identify logical fragments
Credit lifecycle: allocate(provisional) -> periodic_checkpoint(commit_partial) -> finalize(commit_remaining) OR rollback(abort)

Soft quota enforcement: provisional credits decrement available_burst window but do not reduce committed_quota until checkpoint commit; this allows in-flight peak protection without finalizing billing until output completion

Backpressure integration: when provisional allocations exceed in-flight memory/cpu thresholds, apply timed backpressure (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) rather than immediately finalizing commits, to avoid cascade retries

Interaction with streaming fallback: when routing falls back to a cheaper/shorter model midstream, we instantiate a compensation delta that is applied at next checkpoint rather than immediately refunding earlier provisional credits
Migration path: new requests opt-in via header X-RW-HYBRID-METER=1; after 2 weeks of canary we flip default for all streaming and multipart endpoints
Data retention: provisional records expire after 7 days with reconciliation job to surface orphaned provisional allocations for manual review
implementation_steps: Schema: add provisional_credit table (request_id, checkpoint_id, provisional_tokens, status, last_seen) and Redis cache mapping for hot-path
Metering pipeline changes: before emitting final token events, consume provisional allocations; commit emits final_accounting event and tombstones provisional row
Rate limiter: augment token bucket to account for provisional allocations against an ephemeral window and block only when provisional+committed > hard_quota
Client changes: support X-RW-CHKPOINT header to mark explicit partial-commit opportunities; SDKs expose checkpoint() helper
Instrumentation: add Prometheus metrics provisional_allocated_tokens, provisional_committed_tokens, provisional_rollbacks, orphaned_provisionals
E2E tests: create harness that simulates pause/reconnect/replay and asserts single final credit per logical output
PRD: document behavior with examples for canary customers and internal teams
Rollout: start Canary on dedicated infra for 48 hours, run reconciliation job, then progressively enable platform-wide
testing_plan: Unit tests for provisional allocation/commit/rollback logic
Integration tests that replay chunk fragments with varying ordering, duplicate fragments, and aborted streams
Load tests to measure memory/latency impact for checkpoint frequency (checkpoint per 1KB, 8KB, 64KB) and choose default
Chaos testing: kill worker mid-commit, then verify reconcilers recover and establish correct committed credits
Billing audit: run synthetic traffic and compare accounting against golden ledger to verify <=0.01% divergence
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Opt-in header for 5% of traffic on dedicated canary region; monitor reconciler and latency impact for 72h
Phase 2 (gradual): Increase to 25% traffic and enable SDK checkpoint helper for customers integrated with multipart APIs
Phase 3 (default): Flip default behavior for all streaming/multipart endpoints; run nightly reconciler to surface leftover provisional records
Rollback: immediate global disable of X-RW-HYBRID-METER header and drain provisional cache; reconciliation will persist until exhausted
